title: SoloScale Month 1 Content Canon
narrative: I wanted automated output, discovered that the upstream evidence and quality system was missing, then learned through building, measuring, and redesigning that AI engineering is the work of balancing quality, factuality, latency, cost, reliability, complexity, and user experience around a useful outcome.

stories.title_cn: 我做完了很多 AI 项目，但最有价值的东西全丢了
stories.working_title_en: I Built the Software, but Lost the Engineering Experience
stories.one_sentence_thesis: Code was preserved, but decisions, failures, verification, and recovery were scattered across chats, PRs, and tools.
stories.original_user_realization: 我做出了代码，但后来发现，真正值钱的工程经验全丢在聊天记录里了。
stories.fact: ChatGPT reasoning, Codex execution, pull requests, CI, debugging, and recovery steps lived in separate systems and became hard to reconstruct after a feature shipped.
stories.architecture: The workflow produced source code and Git history, but had no shared evidence layer for reasoning, failed assumptions, or recovery context.
stories.decision: Treat engineering experience as a reusable asset rather than disposable conversation context.
stories.implementation: BuildLog and later SoloScale introduced structured runs, evidence records, lineage, and reusable projections.
stories.failure: Finishing the feature looked like success even when the most reusable learning had disappeared.
stories.evolution: Capture the smallest trustworthy evidence package while work happens, then project it into learning, career, and content workflows.
stories.higher_level_insight: Software artifacts are not the full value of engineering work; without evidence, AI-assisted development can become disposable labor.
stories.audience_value: Shows solo builders how to preserve the reasoning and failure knowledge that code alone cannot explain.
overclaim_guardrails: Do not claim every historical decision was captured
Do not claim lost conversations were recovered
stories.video_hook: 我做出了代码，但真正值钱的工程经验全丢在聊天记录里了。
stories.blog_thesis: Engineering memory needs a first-class evidence layer, not another folder of finished code.
stories.linkedin_angle: The uncomfortable moment when shipping revealed that the learning had vanished.
stories.x_thread_angle: Code shipped; context disappeared; evidence became a product requirement.
stories.interview_angle: Explain why SoloScale treats decisions, failures, and recovery as reusable system artifacts.
recommended_visuals: chat, PR, CI, and Git islands

stories.title_cn: 从 AI Research Assistant 到 Personal AI OS
stories.working_title_en: Why My RAG App Turned Into a Personal AI Operating System
stories.one_sentence_thesis: A single RAG feature became a control problem across reasoning, execution, verification, files, and human decisions.
stories.original_user_realization: 我本来只想做一个 RAG 应用，为什么最后做成了一个 AI OS？
stories.fact: The project expanded from research assistance into coordinating ChatGPT, Codex, local files, verification, learning, resume, and content workflows.
stories.architecture: Multiple intelligent tools had different data, permissions, runtimes, and failure modes without a common control plane.
stories.decision: Add typed handoffs and deterministic control instead of asking one chat session to remember everything.
stories.implementation: SoloScale added task envelopes, route decisions, execution packets, evidence, product projections, and human gates.
stories.failure: Adding features to the original RAG app did not solve orchestration or authority boundaries.
stories.evolution: Keep domain capabilities modular while presenting one user-facing operating system.
stories.higher_level_insight: When the problem becomes coordination among intelligent tools and human choices, the missing layer is a control plane.
stories.audience_value: Helps builders recognize when an AI feature has become an orchestration product.
overclaim_guardrails: Do not portray the current local product as a general-purpose operating system
Do not invent the exact date of the transition
stories.video_hook: 我本来只想做一个 RAG 应用，为什么最后做成了一个 AI OS？
stories.blog_thesis: Feature growth and control-plane growth are different architectural transitions.
stories.linkedin_angle: A project changed categories before I noticed.
stories.x_thread_angle: RAG app to control plane in six architectural pressure points.
stories.interview_angle: Describe the signals that caused the architecture to move beyond a single RAG workflow.
recommended_visuals: RAG box expanding into multiple tools

stories.title_cn: AI Agent 的核心不是多放几个 Agent
stories.working_title_en: More Agents Did Not Make My System More Intelligent
stories.one_sentence_thesis: Agent quality came from explicit state, authority, verification, and human gates—not from adding more personas.
stories.original_user_realization: 我一开始以为 Agent 越多越强，最后却删掉了大部分 Agent。
stories.fact: Early designs considered planners, executors, reviewers, critics, and other roles before converging on fewer bounded responsibilities.
stories.architecture: The smaller design separates reasoning, execution, independent verification, deterministic state, and human approval.
stories.decision: Add a role only when it owns a distinct tool, permission boundary, data source, or independently testable result.
stories.implementation: Task envelopes, route decisions, execution packets, state transitions, and explicit gates replaced open-ended agent debate.
stories.failure: More roles repeated context and increased coordination cost without increasing independent evidence.
stories.evolution: Optimize the control flow first; add specialists only when a measurable boundary requires one.
stories.higher_level_insight: An agent system is defined by control flow and authority, not its headcount.
stories.audience_value: Gives teams a practical test for whether another agent role is justified.
overclaim_guardrails: Do not claim multi-agent systems are always inferior
Do not claim every earlier role was implemented
stories.video_hook: 我一开始以为 Agent 越多越强，最后却删掉了大部分 Agent。
stories.blog_thesis: Agent topology should follow independent value and authority boundaries.
stories.linkedin_angle: Deleting agents improved the design because it clarified ownership.
stories.x_thread_angle: Five questions to ask before adding another agent.
stories.interview_angle: Defend why SoloScale uses bounded roles and code-controlled state.

stories.title_cn: Build once. Verify once. Compound everywhere.
stories.working_title_en: One Engineering Experience Should Become Many Career Assets
stories.one_sentence_thesis: One verified engineering experience should support career, learning, content, and interview projections without being reinvented.
stories.original_user_realization: 为什么同一次工程经历，应该同时变成简历、面试和内容？
stories.fact: The same engineering event later needed to support a resume bullet, interview answer, learning case, post, video, thread, and portfolio explanation.
stories.architecture: A shared evidence core can feed multiple domain-specific projections while each product keeps its own approval boundary.
stories.decision: Verify the underlying experience once, then adapt its presentation for each outcome.
stories.implementation: Resume, Learning, Content, BuildLog, and Evidence boundaries were connected through lineage rather than shared prose.
stories.failure: Regenerating each asset from a blank prompt repeated work and created inconsistent claims.
stories.evolution: Measure whether one verified event actually reduces edit time across downstream assets.
stories.higher_level_insight: Build once. Verify once. Compound everywhere.
stories.audience_value: Offers a reusable model for turning real work into durable professional leverage.
overclaim_guardrails: Treat compounding as a product thesis, not a measured business result
Do not imply all projections are fully automated
stories.video_hook: 同一次工程经历，为什么我要重复写七遍？
stories.blog_thesis: The reusable unit is verified experience, not channel-specific copy.
stories.linkedin_angle: A personal workflow became a compounding system design.
stories.x_thread_angle: One engineering event, seven controlled projections.
stories.interview_angle: Explain how shared evidence prevents inconsistent career and content claims.
recommended_visuals: one evidence node branching into seven assets

stories.title_cn: 聊天记录不是知识库
stories.working_title_en: I Connected My Chat History to RAG and Learned That Chat Logs Are Not Knowledge
stories.one_sentence_thesis: Conversation data becomes usable knowledge only after identity, normalization, scope, lineage, and trust are explicit.
stories.original_user_realization: 我把聊天记录接进 RAG 后，才发现聊天记录根本不是知识库。
stories.fact: ChatGPT and Codex exports contained branches, hidden records, tool output, repeated context, format differences, and noise.
stories.architecture: Source adapters normalize records into stable documents and chunks before a private FTS and metadata retrieval layer can use them.
stories.decision: Preserve source identity and active-branch semantics before optimizing embeddings or model quality.
stories.implementation: The Conversation RAG slice added defensive adapters, stable IDs, hashes, redaction, private indexing, and explicit rescans.
stories.failure: Treating an export as a clean corpus would have indexed duplicates, sibling branches, hidden data, and untrusted tool output.
stories.evolution: Improve semantic retrieval only after the source and lineage contract remains deterministic.
stories.higher_level_insight: Data existing does not make it knowledge; knowledge begins with identity and trust boundaries.
stories.audience_value: Provides a concrete ingestion checklist for anyone building RAG over conversation history.
overclaim_guardrails: Do not claim redaction is complete
Do not claim semantic quality from retrieval-only fixtures
stories.video_hook: 我把聊天记录接进 RAG 后，才发现聊天记录根本不是知识库。
stories.blog_thesis: Conversation RAG is an ingestion and trust problem before it is an embedding problem.
stories.linkedin_angle: The messiest part of personal knowledge was upstream of retrieval.
stories.x_thread_angle: Five reasons a chat export is not a knowledge base.
stories.interview_angle: Walk through stable identity, branching, redaction, indexing, and lineage choices.

stories.title_cn: RAG 找到的内容为什么不能直接成为事实
stories.working_title_en: Relevant Retrieval Is Not the Same as Verified Truth
stories.one_sentence_thesis: A relevant search result is a candidate for review, not proof that a career claim is true.
stories.original_user_realization: RAG 最大的幻觉，不一定来自模型，而是我们误把‘相关’当成‘真实’。
stories.fact: Search could retrieve code or conversations related to a skill without proving that the candidate completed the work or mastered it.
stories.architecture: Retrieved candidates, verified evidence, and approved career claims occupy different states with an explicit promotion boundary.
stories.decision: Prevent retrieval output from flowing directly into resumes or mastery records.
stories.implementation: Evidence candidates retain lineage; Resume uses approved profile facts; Learning keeps engineering verification separate from human mastery.
stories.failure: High lexical relevance was easy to mistake for semantic support and ownership.
stories.evolution: Make candidate, verified, and approved states visible wherever retrieved evidence influences a user outcome.
stories.higher_level_insight: Retrieved candidate is not verified evidence, and verified evidence is not automatically an approved claim.
stories.audience_value: Clarifies a common but dangerous truth-boundary mistake in career and knowledge products.
overclaim_guardrails: Do not claim retrieval is unreliable in general
Do not imply human review proves ownership without evidence
stories.video_hook: RAG 找到了相关内容，为什么我还是不敢把它写进简历？
stories.blog_thesis: Retrieval relevance and claim truth need separate contracts.
stories.linkedin_angle: The most dangerous hallucination happened between subsystems, not inside the model.
stories.x_thread_angle: Candidate, evidence, claim: three states that should never collapse.
stories.interview_angle: Defend the promotion boundary between knowledge retrieval and career claims.
recommended_visuals: blocked arrow from RAG to Resume

stories.title_cn: 我做简历生成器后，才真正理解 Truth Boundary
stories.working_title_en: A Prompt Cannot Prevent Resume Hallucinations
stories.one_sentence_thesis: Resume truth requires evidence, typed claims, validation, fallback, and human review—not one prompt instruction.
stories.original_user_realization: 为什么一句‘不要编造’，解决不了 AI 简历幻觉？
stories.fact: Candidate rewrites could turn contribution into leadership, prototypes into production, or add unsupported metrics and outcomes.
stories.architecture: Approved source facts feed structured model output, deterministic validation, claim-level fallback, provenance, and a final human review state.
stories.decision: Make truth a system contract and preserve useful rewrites only when their factual content remains supported.
stories.implementation: SoloScale added claim statuses, source IDs, rejected-candidate persistence, provenance, and selective fallback.
stories.failure: A strong instruction could not prevent a capable model from optimizing beyond the factual boundary.
stories.evolution: Permit richer evidence-backed synthesis while continuing to reject new ownership, scale, customers, technologies, numbers, and outcomes.
stories.higher_level_insight: Do not hallucinate is not a prompt; it is an end-to-end product contract.
stories.audience_value: Shows how to combine model creativity with deterministic career-fact safety.
overclaim_guardrails: Do not call a structurally valid response truthful
Do not claim the validator catches every semantic inflation
stories.video_hook: 为什么一句‘不要编造’，解决不了 AI 简历幻觉？
stories.blog_thesis: Career AI needs a deterministic shell around probabilistic writing.
stories.linkedin_angle: The prompt was the smallest part of the truth system.
stories.x_thread_angle: Six layers between a resume fact and an exported DOCX.
stories.interview_angle: Explain the validator, fallback, provenance, and human gate as one safety boundary.

stories.title_cn: 简历需要包装，但包装和造假的边界在哪里
stories.working_title_en: A Resume Is Not a Transcript—but It Cannot Become Fiction
stories.one_sentence_thesis: Resume writing should maximize positioning through supported synthesis while forbidding new material facts.
stories.original_user_realization: 简历当然需要包装，但什么时候包装开始变成幻觉？
stories.fact: An overly lexical validator preserved truth but also rejected professional phrasing and reasonable summaries supported by multiple facts.
stories.architecture: Atomic facts and explicit evidence IDs can support rewrite, synthesis, prioritization, and compression inside a fixed factual boundary.
stories.decision: Allow presentation enhancement and bounded inference; forbid new metrics, ownership, scale, customers, technologies, and outcomes.
stories.implementation: The current whole-resume contract introduced multi-source synthesis fields, Summary rewriting, ordering, and item-level fallback.
stories.failure: Safety optimized as lexical similarity produced a resume that was safe but barely different.
stories.evolution: Judge each atomic fact and provenance set, then measure whether the final resume is both defensible and materially stronger.
stories.higher_level_insight: A resume is synthesis, not transcription, but synthesis must remain explainable from real facts.
stories.audience_value: Gives builders a practical boundary between strong positioning and fabrication.
overclaim_guardrails: Do not describe the current synthesis acceptance as successful
Do not relax role or metric checks to increase pass rate
stories.video_hook: 简历需要包装，但包装和幻觉的边界到底在哪里？
stories.blog_thesis: Truth-constrained synthesis is the core writing problem in an AI resume product.
stories.linkedin_angle: Safety worked; usefulness did not—so the contract had to evolve.
stories.x_thread_angle: What a resume model may change, infer, and never invent.
stories.interview_angle: Discuss atomic claims, multi-source synthesis, and safe fallback trade-offs.

stories.title_cn: AI Coding 速度带来的 Learning Debt
stories.working_title_en: AI Helped Me Build Faster Than I Could Learn
stories.one_sentence_thesis: AI reduced implementation latency while the builder's understanding lagged behind the evolving codebase.
stories.original_user_realization: AI 帮我越写越快，我为什么反而越来越不懂自己的项目？
stories.fact: Codex could implement features faster than the operator could reconstruct every architectural decision and code path.
stories.architecture: Engineering completion and human mastery are stored as separate states in Learning Tower.
stories.decision: Do not let passing tests or existing code automatically promote human mastery.
stories.implementation: Learning Traceability links evidence, decisions, code, tests, and Explain or Trace exercises without auto-grading mastery.
stories.failure: More shipped code created a false sense of progress while interview defensibility lagged.
stories.evolution: Use selected project claims to drive focused Explain, Trace, Rebuild, Debug, and Defend practice.
stories.higher_level_insight: Code existence proves engineering state; it does not prove human understanding.
stories.audience_value: Names a hidden cost of AI coding and offers a measurable way to manage it.
overclaim_guardrails: Keep the learning gap as the user's interpretation
Do not claim objective mastery decline without assessment data
stories.video_hook: AI 帮我越写越快，我为什么反而越来越不懂自己的项目？
stories.blog_thesis: AI coding creates a new form of comprehension debt that needs its own state model.
stories.linkedin_angle: Shipping faster exposed a gap between project state and personal mastery.
stories.x_thread_angle: Five signs your AI coding velocity is creating learning debt.
stories.interview_angle: Explain why Learning Tower separates engineering evidence from mastery evidence.
recommended_visuals: code velocity rising while mastery lags

stories.title_cn: Resume Bullet 是一份 Interview Contract
stories.working_title_en: Every Resume Bullet Is an Interview Contract
stories.one_sentence_thesis: Every technical term placed on a resume becomes an invitation for deeper questions that the candidate must defend.
stories.original_user_realization: 简历里每多写一个技术名词，面试官就多了一个击穿你的入口。
stories.fact: A resume bullet can trigger questions about architecture, decisions, implementation, failures, trade-offs, and evolution.
stories.architecture: The same claim should resolve to a six-layer engineering story and its code or evidence anchors.
stories.decision: Treat a resume bullet as a technical contract rather than isolated marketing copy.
stories.implementation: Resume provenance and Learning Traceability provide anchors for later interview-defense workflows.
stories.failure: A polished bullet without recoverable technical context increases interview risk.
stories.evolution: Let users jump from a resume claim to Fact, Architecture, Decision, Implementation, Failure, and Evolution practice.
stories.higher_level_insight: A resume bullet is a technical attack surface voluntarily offered to the interviewer.
stories.audience_value: Helps candidates choose claims they can defend and prepare the depth behind them.
overclaim_guardrails: Present attack surface as a metaphor
Do not imply every interviewer asks all six layers
stories.video_hook: 简历里每多写一个技术名词，面试官就多了一个击穿你的入口。
stories.blog_thesis: Career positioning and interview preparation should share one evidence-backed story model.
stories.linkedin_angle: A better bullet can increase both opportunity and scrutiny.
stories.x_thread_angle: Turn one resume bullet into six interview-defense questions.
stories.interview_angle: Use the complete six-layer framework as the answer structure.
recommended_visuals: resume bullet expanding into six questions

stories.title_cn: 技术债不可怕，无法解释的技术债才危险
stories.working_title_en: Technical Debt Is Defendable; Unexplained Debt Is Not
stories.one_sentence_thesis: Technical debt becomes a strong engineering signal when its origin, cost, measurement, and next design are understood.
stories.original_user_realization: 面试时该不该承认项目有技术债？我的答案是：必须承认。
stories.fact: SoloScale accumulated blocking requests, model latency, schema incompatibility, validator false rejections, large modules, and packaging debt.
stories.architecture: Several debts crossed UI, model, validation, storage, and packaging boundaries rather than living in one isolated component.
stories.decision: Record debt as a measured trade-off instead of hiding it behind green tests or polished demos.
stories.implementation: Stage timings, failure categories, rejected outputs, job states, and release checkpoints made selected debt inspectable.
stories.failure: Treating every debt as an immediate refactor repeatedly slowed the user outcome.
stories.evolution: Prioritize debt by user impact and evidence, then explain why the smallest current design was chosen.
stories.higher_level_insight: Technical debt is defendable; unexplained technical debt is not.
stories.audience_value: Shows candidates how to discuss imperfect systems without pretending they are production-perfect.
overclaim_guardrails: Do not claim every debt has been resolved
Do not call local MVP debt a production incident
stories.video_hook: 面试时该不该承认项目有技术债？必须承认。
stories.blog_thesis: The quality of a debt explanation is itself evidence of engineering judgment.
stories.linkedin_angle: What I learned from showing the cracks in a solo AI product.
stories.x_thread_angle: How to explain technical debt with evidence instead of excuses.
stories.interview_angle: Choose one debt and cover cause, cost, measurement, trade-off, and evolution.

stories.title_cn: Backend 能运行，不代表产品能用
stories.working_title_en: My AI Feature Worked, but the Product Still Failed
stories.one_sentence_thesis: Technical feasibility became product value only when a normal user could finish the workflow through the packaged Desktop App.
stories.original_user_realization: 我的 AI 功能早就能跑了，为什么我自己还是不愿意用？
stories.fact: Functions and command-line paths worked while the Desktop product still had navigation, download, preview, WebView, packaging, and state failures.
stories.architecture: A Swift and WKWebView shell launches a packaged Python sidecar and exposes local routes and downloads to a normal user.
stories.decision: Use the packaged App flow—not direct Python calls—as the acceptance boundary for user outcomes.
stories.implementation: Cold-start checks, background jobs, PDF preview, real Downloads verification, and explicit UI states were added and dogfooded.
stories.failure: Backend success repeatedly masked broken user paths that still required a developer or terminal.
stories.evolution: Make each slice prove the final user artifact through the packaged product before treating it as usable.
stories.higher_level_insight: A prototype proves feasibility; product engineering proves a user can reach the outcome independently.
stories.audience_value: Connects backend engineering to the often-missed delivery and usability boundary.
overclaim_guardrails: Describe a local single-user product, not a public release
Do not claim notarization or multi-user readiness
stories.video_hook: 我的 AI 功能早就能跑了，为什么我自己还是不愿意用？
stories.blog_thesis: The user outcome, not the callable function, is the meaningful product boundary.
stories.linkedin_angle: The point where I stopped accepting terminal success as product success.
stories.x_thread_angle: Backend green, product red: five Desktop failure modes.
stories.interview_angle: Describe how packaged App E2E changed the definition of done.

stories.title_cn: 点击 Generate 后，整个 App 卡死两分钟
stories.working_title_en: My AI App Froze for Two Minutes Every Time I Clicked Generate
stories.one_sentence_thesis: A synchronous request coupled model latency to the entire UI lifecycle.
stories.original_user_realization: 我一点 Generate，整个 App 就像死了两分钟。
stories.fact: The old Resume request performed generation, verification, DOCX creation, and PDF preview before returning control to the UI.
stories.architecture: One HTTP request owned both the user interaction lifetime and a long-running local inference pipeline.
stories.decision: Separate request latency, background-job lifetime, artifact readiness, and model latency.
stories.implementation: Resume Job Manager returns a job ID, runs one background worker, exposes polling, and makes DOCX available before PDF preview.
stories.failure: The UI appeared frozen even though the backend was still working correctly.
stories.evolution: Keep measuring model latency separately from product responsiveness and preserve bounded local concurrency.
stories.higher_level_insight: Long-running inference should not control the UI lifecycle.
stories.audience_value: Teaches a small, practical architecture for responsive local AI products.
verified_metrics: Two verified qwen3:8b runs completed in 122.584s and 128.258s
The POST path returned in 19ms and 16ms after the background-job change
overclaim_guardrails: Say the App appeared frozen before the fix, not that the process crashed
Keep the measurements tied to two local runs
stories.video_hook: 我一点 Generate，整个 App 就像死了两分钟。
stories.blog_thesis: UI responsiveness and inference throughput are separate engineering constraints.
stories.linkedin_angle: A visible product failure led to a smaller architecture than Redis or Celery.
stories.x_thread_angle: How one synchronous AI request froze a local product.
stories.interview_angle: Trace the old request path and the new background-job lifecycle.

stories.title_cn: ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1) 背后的设计
stories.working_title_en: Why My AI App Uses Only One Background Worker
stories.one_sentence_thesis: One bounded worker solved UI concurrency without pretending a laptop could run unlimited local inference.
stories.original_user_realization: 为什么我的 AI App 明明支持后台任务，却只允许一个工人？
stories.fact: The local Resume job manager uses a single ThreadPoolExecutor worker and returns job IDs for polling.
stories.architecture: HTTP requests remain responsive while one inference job runs at a time with explicit queued, running, artifact-ready, complete, and failed states.
stories.decision: Choose the lowest-complexity design that provides responsiveness, backpressure, and failure isolation for one local user.
stories.implementation: A Resume Job Manager, one worker, immediate POST response, polling, staged artifacts, and per-phase timings replaced synchronous execution.
stories.failure: Increasing request concurrency would not increase local model capacity and could make latency and memory behavior worse.
stories.evolution: Add stronger queues only when real multi-user demand or multiple execution hosts exist.
stories.higher_level_insight: UI concurrency and AI inference concurrency do not have to be equal.
stories.audience_value: Demonstrates proportionate architecture and explicit backpressure in a local AI product.
overclaim_guardrails: Do not present one worker as universally optimal
Do not describe it as distributed job infrastructure
stories.video_hook: 为什么我的 AI App 支持后台任务，却只允许一个工人？
stories.blog_thesis: Bounded concurrency can be a product feature rather than an infrastructure limitation.
stories.linkedin_angle: The design became better when I resisted adding a queue platform.
stories.x_thread_angle: Why max_workers=1 was an intentional architecture decision.
stories.interview_angle: Defend backpressure, failure isolation, and the trigger for future scaling.

stories.title_cn: 不要猜性能瓶颈，要测
stories.working_title_en: I Blamed RAG for the Latency—Then Measured the Real Bottleneck
stories.one_sentence_thesis: Stage timings showed that local model generation—not retrieval, DOCX, PDF, or request handling—dominated the measured runtime.
stories.original_user_realization: 我以为 RAG 拖慢了 App，测完才发现 99% 时间都花在模型上。
stories.fact: Two completed qwen3:8b Desktop runs attributed more than 99% of total time to model generation.
stories.architecture: The job records post response, profile extraction, retrieval, generation, verification, DOCX, PDF preview, and total duration separately.
stories.decision: Use stage attribution before changing retrieval or document architecture.
stories.implementation: Per-stage timing was persisted in the Resume job receipt and surfaced in the Desktop progress UI.
stories.failure: The initial intuition blamed RAG and the UI even though neither was the measured bottleneck.
stories.evolution: Route future optimization work to the measured model path and retain timings as regression evidence.
stories.higher_level_insight: Performance engineering begins with attribution, not optimization.
stories.audience_value: Shows how small observability changed an architectural decision and prevented wasted work.
verified_metrics: Generation share exceeded 99% in both measured runs
overclaim_guardrails: Describe two local measurements, not a benchmark percentile
Do not generalize the bottleneck to other models or machines
stories.video_hook: 我以为 RAG 拖慢了 App，测完才发现 99% 时间都花在模型上。
stories.blog_thesis: A seven-field timing receipt prevented an unnecessary retrieval redesign.
stories.linkedin_angle: The cheapest observability delivered the highest-value architecture decision.
stories.x_thread_angle: What I measured before touching the RAG pipeline.
stories.interview_angle: Present the timing breakdown, hypothesis change, and resulting optimization priority.

stories.title_cn: qwen 从 97 秒压到 59 秒，我为什么回滚了
stories.working_title_en: I Made the Model Faster and Rejected the Optimization
stories.one_sentence_thesis: A faster output contract removed the meaningful rewrite value the user was waiting for.
stories.original_user_realization: 我把 AI 加速了，为什么最后却决定不要这个优化？
stories.fact: A compact local-model experiment appeared materially faster but returned no substantive resume rewrites.
stories.architecture: The prompt, schema, and output budget controlled both model latency and the richness of the candidate rewrite.
stories.decision: Reject a component-level speed improvement when the user-facing outcome regresses.
stories.implementation: The experiment compared the same resume task under the baseline and compact contracts with truth validation retained.
stories.failure: Latency improved while the product value collapsed to conservative or unchanged output.
stories.evolution: Compare latency, accepted material rewrites, truth, and user preference together rather than optimizing one metric.
stories.higher_level_insight: Lower latency is not progress when it removes the reason the user waits.
stories.audience_value: Explains why local optimization needs an outcome metric, not only a stopwatch.
overclaim_guardrails: Do not publish 96.7s or 59.3s until matching receipts are linked
Do not call the experiment a general model benchmark
stories.video_hook: 我把 AI 加速了，为什么最后却决定不要这个优化？
stories.blog_thesis: Performance work must be evaluated against the product outcome it is supposed to accelerate.
stories.linkedin_angle: The optimization passed the stopwatch and failed the user.
stories.x_thread_angle: A speed win that produced zero meaningful rewrites.
stories.interview_angle: Explain the rejected optimization and the missing product metric.

stories.title_cn: 本地模型免费但慢，Sol 几分钱却快很多
stories.working_title_en: I Saved a Few Cents and Made the User Wait Much Longer
stories.one_sentence_thesis: Model routing is a product trade-off across quality, latency, cost, factuality, privacy, and user value.
stories.original_user_realization: 为了省几分钱，我让用户多等了一分多钟，这真的是优化吗？
stories.fact: Local qwen was free and slow; hosted Sol returned much faster and proposed stronger rewrites but crossed truth boundaries more often.
stories.architecture: Local retrieval and truth enforcement can remain deterministic while high-value writing routes to a hosted model.
stories.decision: Compare models by usable final output, latency, cost, and factual safety instead of local-versus-cloud ideology.
stories.implementation: A bounded A/B used one request per model, reasoning disabled, no retries, and the same truth contract.
stories.failure: The cheaper route optimized API spend while imposing a much larger waiting and quality cost on the user.
stories.evolution: Use Sol for high-value positioning, keep qwen as an offline option, and persist exact usage when choosing defaults.
stories.higher_level_insight: The cheapest model call can be the most expensive product choice.
stories.audience_value: Gives builders a practical framework for routing local and hosted models.
overclaim_guardrails: Do not publish exact cost without the matching usage receipt
Do not imply Sol is always more truthful or faster
stories.video_hook: 为了省几分钱，我让用户多等了一分多钟，这真的是优化吗？
stories.blog_thesis: Model selection belongs to product economics, not only infrastructure configuration.
stories.linkedin_angle: A few cents changed the quality and waiting-time equation.
stories.x_thread_angle: Local versus hosted across six product dimensions.
stories.interview_angle: Defend the routing decision and the continuing deterministic truth boundary.

stories.title_cn: Provider Schema 不等于 Domain Contract
stories.working_title_en: A JSON Schema Error Taught Me to Separate Provider and Domain Contracts
stories.one_sentence_thesis: Provider-compatible wire schemas should not weaken the product's canonical truth rules.
stories.original_user_realization: 一个 uniqueItems 错误，让我理解了 Provider Contract 和 Domain Contract 的区别。
stories.fact: A hosted-model request failed before generation because a strict provider schema rejected a constraint SoloScale still needed locally.
stories.architecture: SoloScale keeps a canonical domain contract, projects a provider-compatible wire schema, then applies deterministic local validation.
stories.decision: Adapt transport constraints at the boundary without letting a provider redefine internal truth and business rules.
stories.implementation: The gateway added a canonical-to-wire schema projection while retaining local uniqueness and reference checks.
stories.failure: Sending the internal schema directly made provider compatibility look like a model-quality failure.
stories.evolution: Treat each provider as a wire-format dependency and preserve one stable domain contract behind it.
stories.higher_level_insight: A provider controls the format it accepts, not the product truth it should enforce.
stories.audience_value: Shows how to isolate provider quirks without scattering business rules across adapters.
overclaim_guardrails: Do not describe the error as model execution
Do not claim universal JSON Schema incompatibility
stories.video_hook: 一个 uniqueItems 错误，让我理解了 Provider Contract 和 Domain Contract 的区别。
stories.blog_thesis: Wire compatibility and domain correctness require separate schemas and ownership.
stories.linkedin_angle: A small 400 error exposed the wrong dependency direction.
stories.x_thread_angle: Provider schema versus product contract in one failure trace.
stories.interview_angle: Explain the adapter boundary and why local validation remains authoritative.

stories.chapter: Failure Isolation, Career Systems, and Content Compounding
stories.title_cn: 一条错误不应该让整份 AI 输出报废
stories.working_title_en: Four Good Rewrites and Four Bad Ones Should Not Equal Zero
stories.one_sentence_thesis: Fail-closed systems can isolate failure at claim level instead of discarding every valid part of a document.
stories.original_user_realization: AI 写对了一半，为什么我的系统却把整份结果都扔了？
stories.fact: A Sol candidate contained both truth-safe and rejected rewrites, while the earlier document-level validator discarded the whole result.
stories.architecture: Each candidate rewrite now validates independently and falls back to the original approved bullet when rejected.
stories.decision: Keep the final document fact-safe while accepting useful model output at the smallest safe unit.
stories.implementation: Selective rewrite tracks accepted and rejected candidates and builds the final DOCX from accepted text plus original fallbacks.
stories.failure: Document-level fail-closed behavior turned partial model value into zero usable output.
stories.evolution: Extend the same isolation principle to supported multi-source synthesis and section-level editing.
stories.higher_level_insight: Fail-closed does not require fail-everything.
stories.audience_value: Offers a reusable failure-isolation pattern for structured generative workflows.
overclaim_guardrails: Do not publish four-and-four counts until the matching run receipt is linked
Do not claim rejected text entered the exported resume
stories.video_hook: AI 写对了一半，为什么我的系统却把整份结果都扔了？
stories.blog_thesis: The safe unit of failure should be smaller than the unit of user value.
stories.linkedin_angle: A strict safety design was correct at the wrong granularity.
stories.x_thread_angle: From document-level rejection to claim-level fallback.
stories.interview_angle: Explain how selective fallback preserves both truth and partial model value.

stories.chapter: Failure Isolation, Career Systems, and Content Compounding
stories.title_cn: 为什么被拒绝的 AI 输出也应该保存
stories.working_title_en: Rejected AI Output Is Still Valuable Engineering Data
stories.one_sentence_thesis: Rejected content must stay out of the product while remaining available as local diagnostic evidence.
stories.original_user_realization: 我为了找回一条几美分的 AI 响应，差点浪费了更多时间和 token。
stories.fact: A rejected Sol response was lost before persistence, and attempts to recover it consumed more effort than the original request.
stories.architecture: The improved path persists a structured candidate before truth validation and marks failures REJECTED and NOT FOR SUBMISSION.
stories.decision: Separate product eligibility from observability value.
stories.implementation: Pre-validation candidate persistence provides offline inspection without another paid model call.
stories.failure: Failing safely also destroyed the evidence needed to understand whether the validator or model was wrong.
stories.evolution: Retain bounded, private, clearly ineligible failure artifacts for diagnosis and contract improvement.
stories.higher_level_insight: Rejected output is not product output, but it is valuable engineering data.
stories.audience_value: Shows how failure persistence prevents repeat spending and blind validator changes.
overclaim_guardrails: Do not publish the rejected candidate body
Keep cost references approximate unless a usage receipt exists
stories.video_hook: 我为了找回一条几美分的 AI 响应，差点浪费了更多时间。
stories.blog_thesis: Failure isolation needs durable diagnostic output as well as safe product fallback.
stories.linkedin_angle: The response was cheap; the missing observability was expensive.
stories.x_thread_angle: Why rejected AI output should be saved but never shipped.
stories.interview_angle: Discuss the distinction between persistence, eligibility, and publication.

stories.chapter: Failure Isolation, Career Systems, and Content Compounding
stories.title_cn: Application Resume 和 Target Benchmark Resume 为什么要分开
stories.working_title_en: Why My Resume System Generates One Resume I Can Use and One I Must Never Submit
stories.one_sentence_thesis: What I can truthfully submit today and what an ideal candidate would show are different product questions.
stories.original_user_realization: 为什么我决定让 AI 同时生成一份能投的简历，和一份绝对不能投的简历？
stories.fact: A truth-constrained Application Resume and an aspirational market benchmark serve different user decisions.
stories.architecture: Verified evidence feeds the submittable resume; the JD-optimal benchmark is explicitly separated and feeds a gap engine instead.
stories.decision: Never mix aspirational capabilities into the application artifact.
stories.implementation: The Application Resume boundary exists; the Target Benchmark and gap workflow remain a planned product slice.
stories.failure: One document could not safely optimize both present truth and future aspiration.
stories.evolution: Compare reality and target, then turn each gap into Learn, Build, Reframe, Interview, or Evidence work.
stories.higher_level_insight: Truthful application and market benchmark should be connected but never conflated.
stories.audience_value: Transforms resume generation into a career-development feedback system without encouraging fabrication.
overclaim_guardrails: Mark Target Benchmark NOT FOR SUBMISSION
Describe benchmark and gap automation as planned until implemented
stories.video_hook: 为什么一份简历可以投，另一份必须永远不能投？
stories.blog_thesis: Separating reality from aspiration creates a safer and more useful career product.
stories.linkedin_angle: The second resume is valuable precisely because it cannot be submitted.
stories.x_thread_angle: Application versus benchmark in one career feedback loop.
stories.interview_angle: Explain the boundary and how gaps become learning or project tasks.

stories.chapter: Failure Isolation, Career Systems, and Content Compounding
stories.title_cn: 六层技术深挖本身就是 Content Framework
stories.working_title_en: My Interview Preparation Framework Became My Content Framework
stories.one_sentence_thesis: Fact, Architecture, Decision, Implementation, Failure, and Evolution can drive both interview defense and technical storytelling.
stories.original_user_realization: 我发现技术面试的准备框架，本身就是最好的内容生产框架。
stories.fact: The same depth needed to defend a project in an interview also structures a video, blog, post, thread, and portfolio case study.
stories.architecture: One canonical Engineering Story stores six layers and projects them into channel-specific artifacts.
stories.decision: Share the deep understanding model while keeping each output format and approval flow separate.
stories.implementation: The first evidence-backed local video uses a SixLayerStory and verified evidence before scenes and narration are rendered.
stories.failure: Separate interview notes and content prompts repeatedly rediscovered the same architecture and trade-offs.
stories.evolution: Let every canonical Month 1 story feed Learning, Video, Blog, LinkedIn, X, and portfolio outputs without copying prose blindly.
stories.higher_level_insight: Interview Defense and Content Production are different projections of the same understood engineering story.
stories.audience_value: Provides one practical framework for learning deeply and publishing credibly.
overclaim_guardrails: Do not claim all projections are automated
Do not treat the six layers as proof of mastery without user practice
stories.video_hook: 我发现技术面试的准备框架，本身就是最好的内容生产框架。
stories.blog_thesis: Deep technical understanding is the reusable source asset behind both interviews and content.
stories.linkedin_angle: One framework eliminated duplicate preparation work.
stories.x_thread_angle: Six layers that turn one project into defensible content.
stories.interview_angle: Use the six layers directly to defend the first video story.
recommended_visuals: one story branching into interview and content

stories.chapter: Failure Isolation, Career Systems, and Content Compounding
stories.title_cn: 我本来想每天发内容，一个月后却几乎没有稳定产出
stories.working_title_en: I Tried to Automate Daily Content and Discovered That Automation Does Not Create Quality
stories.one_sentence_thesis: Automation could amplify throughput only after evidence, story structure, user flow, and quality standards became usable.
stories.original_user_realization: 我本来想用 AI 每天发内容，一个月后却发现真正的瓶颈根本不是写作。
stories.fact: The original goal was daily multi-platform publishing, while actual output remained low or weak during the upstream product build.
stories.architecture: Content quality depended on evidence capture, canonical stories, review, channel adaptation, visuals, approval, publishing, and receipts.
stories.decision: Stop treating draft generation as the bottleneck and strengthen the upstream story and evidence system.
stories.implementation: Content Studio, review, BuildLog handoff, Video Factory, Reference Intelligence, and this Month 1 canon were built as controlled stages.
stories.failure: Automating weak or missing input only produced weak output more efficiently.
stories.evolution: Use the real engineering process as the content source, publish a smaller coherent canon, and learn from audience response.
stories.higher_level_insight: Automation increases throughput; it does not create quality.
stories.audience_value: Offers an honest counterpoint to generic claims that AI alone creates a content engine.
overclaim_guardrails: The low-output assessment is the user's interpretation
Do not invent publication counts or engagement
stories.video_hook: 我本来想用 AI 每天发内容，一个月后却发现瓶颈根本不是写作。
stories.blog_thesis: A content engine is only as strong as its upstream evidence and editorial judgment.
stories.linkedin_angle: The gap between an automation plan and one month of real output.
stories.x_thread_angle: Why content automation failed before it began.
stories.interview_angle: Describe how user outcome redirected the product roadmap.

stories.chapter: Failure Isolation, Career Systems, and Content Compounding
stories.title_cn: AI Engineering 本质上是在寻找可接受的 Outcome
stories.working_title_en: What One Month of Building Taught Me About AI Engineering
stories.one_sentence_thesis: AI engineering is the continuous work of balancing system trade-offs around a clearly defined useful outcome.
stories.original_user_realization: 做了一个月 AI 产品后，我才真正理解 AI Engineering 是什么。
stories.fact: SoloScale repeatedly exposed trade-offs among local and hosted models, latency, cost, truth, output quality, UX, testing, speed, and architecture complexity.
stories.architecture: Deterministic evidence, validation, and state surround probabilistic models selected for different judgment and generation tasks.
stories.decision: Define the user outcome first, measure the weakest stage, and add only the complexity needed to reach an acceptable operating point.
stories.implementation: The project iterated through evidence, Resume, Learning, Content, Desktop delivery, performance timing, model routing, and failure isolation.
stories.failure: Optimizing architecture, tests, speed, or cost in isolation repeatedly missed the actual user outcome.
stories.evolution: Use real applications, interviews, publications, and user judgment to decide the next smallest engineering change.
stories.higher_level_insight: AI engineering is not choosing the strongest model; it is balancing quality, factuality, latency, cost, reliability, flexibility, complexity, and UX until the outcome is useful.
stories.audience_value: Closes Month 1 with a practical definition grounded in one product's repeated trade-offs.
overclaim_guardrails: Present this as the builder's learned definition
Do not claim the system has reached a production optimum
stories.video_hook: 做了一个月 AI 产品后，我才真正理解 AI Engineering 是什么。
stories.blog_thesis: AI engineering is outcome optimization under interacting technical and product constraints.
stories.linkedin_angle: The final lesson was not about a model; it was about the operating point of the whole system.
stories.x_thread_angle: Eight trade-offs that changed my definition of AI engineering.
stories.interview_angle: Use the month as a coherent systems-design and product-judgment case study.
